blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Concrete Driveway Cost in Geelong in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Planning a new concrete driveway in Geelong? We break down the real costs, pricing factors, and what to expect for your budget in 2026.
body: If you are a Geelong homeowner thinking about a new concrete driveway, one of the first questions on your mind is probably how much this is going to cost. The truth is, concrete driveway costs in Geelong vary depending on several key factors including the size of your driveway, the type of finish you choose, site access, and ground conditions. In 2026, most Geelong homeowners can expect to pay between $5,000 and $12,000 for a standard residential concrete driveway, with premium finishes like exposed aggregate pushing that figure higher. Understanding these cost drivers before you request quotes from Geelong concreters will help you budget accurately and avoid surprises.

The type of concrete finish you select has the biggest impact on your final price. A basic brushed concrete driveway is the most affordable option, typically starting from around $5,000 for a standard double driveway in Geelong. Exposed aggregate, which reveals the natural stone beneath the surface, generally costs between $8,000 and $14,000 depending on the aggregate mix and area size. Stamped or patterned concrete, which mimics the look of pavers or natural stone, falls somewhere in between these figures. At Olson Concreting, we walk Geelong clients through every finish option so you can choose a surface that suits both your home and your budget.

Site conditions play a major role in what you will pay for your Geelong driveway. Geelong's western suburbs like Highton and Belmont often sit on heavier clay soils, which require more excavation and preparation before pouring. If your driveway has poor drainage or sits on a slope, additional groundwork may be needed, adding to the overall cost. Access is another factor — if machinery cannot easily reach the pour site, more manual labour is required. At Olson Concreting, we assess all of these variables during our free on-site quote in Geelong, so there are no nasty surprises once the project begins.

Australian Standards require concrete driveways to be at least 100mm thick for residential use, with proper reinforcement and a compacted base. In Geelong, where we experience everything from scorching summer days to cold, wet winters, getting the mix and thickness right is critical. Using a lower-quality concrete mix to save money upfront often leads to cracking and deterioration within just a few years. We always recommend using a minimum 32MPa concrete mix for driveways in the Geelong region, which provides the durability needed to handle local traffic loads and the region's variable weather conditions throughout the year.

Another cost factor many Geelong homeowners overlook is the finishing and edges. Simple square edges are the most cost-effective, while rounded or bullnose edges add a premium touch at a modest additional cost. Coloured concrete, where pigment is mixed throughout the slab, adds roughly 15 to 25 percent to the base price. Sealing your driveway after completion is also strongly recommended in Geelong's coastal environment to protect against salt air and moisture penetration. A quality sealer application typically costs between $300 and $600 for an average-sized driveway, but it significantly extends the life of your concrete investment.

At Olson Concreting, we provide every Geelong client with a detailed, fixed-price quote before any work begins. This quote covers all excavation, preparation, materials, pouring, finishing, and cleanup — so the price we quote is the price you pay. We have been concreting driveways across Geelong and the Bellarine Peninsula for over a decade, and we know exactly what it takes to deliver a driveway that looks great and lasts for years. Contact us today for a free, no-obligation quote on your new concrete driveway in Geelong.

blogPosts.title: Best Time to Pour Concrete in Geelong's Variable Climate
blogPosts.excerpt: Geelong's weather can be unpredictable. Learn the best seasons and conditions for pouring concrete to ensure a lasting, crack-free finish.
body: Geelong enjoys a temperate oceanic climate, but that does not mean it is always ideal for pouring concrete. The coastal city experiences warm, dry summers, cool and sometimes wet winters, and everything in between. Pouring concrete in the wrong conditions can lead to poor curing, surface cracking, and a driveway or slab that does not stand the test of time. If you are planning a concreting project in Geelong, understanding the best time of year to pour is one of the most important steps you can take to protect your investment and ensure long-lasting results.

The optimal time to pour concrete in Geelong is during the drier months between October and April, when daytime temperatures sit between 15 and 30 degrees Celsius. These conditions allow the concrete to cure gradually and evenly, which is essential for achieving maximum strength. Spring and early autumn are often considered the sweet spot, as the weather is typically warm enough for proper curing without the extreme heat that can cause rapid moisture loss. At Olson Concreting, we schedule most of our Geelong driveway projects during these months to ensure the best possible outcome for our clients.

Summer pouring in Geelong requires careful planning and experience. While the warm temperatures are generally favourable, the hot north winds that occasionally sweep through the region can cause the surface moisture to evaporate too quickly, leading to surface cracks and a weakened finish. We counter this by dampening the surface and using curing compounds during hot Geelong days. Midday pours are generally avoided during peak summer, with early morning starts preferred to take advantage of cooler temperatures. If you are planning a summer concrete project in Geelong, choosing an experienced concreter who understands these local conditions makes all the difference.

Winter concreting in Geelong is more challenging but not impossible with the right approach. The cooler temperatures between June and August slow down the curing process significantly, which means the concrete needs more time to reach its full design strength. Frost is rare in Geelong but not unheard of, and any freezing temperatures can seriously damage freshly poured concrete. If a winter pour is necessary, we use accelerated curing techniques and insulating blankets to protect the slab. Rain is the bigger concern during Geelong winters, so we closely monitor forecasts and only pour when we are confident of a sustained dry window.

Soil conditions in the Geelong region also influence the ideal timing for your concrete project. Many areas, particularly in suburbs like Highton, Belmont, and Grovedale, sit on reactive clay soils that expand and contract with moisture changes throughout the year. Pouring a concrete driveway on unstable or waterlogged ground can lead to subsidence and cracking over time. The ideal time to address this is during the drier months when the soil is more stable and predictable. At Olson Concreting, we always assess ground conditions as part of our free on-site quote in Geelong, ensuring your new driveway or slab is built on a solid foundation regardless of when you choose to pour.

Ultimately, the best time to pour concrete in Geelong is when conditions are right for your specific site and project scope. Working with a local concreter who understands Geelong's unique climate, soil conditions, and coastal exposure ensures your project is timed and executed for the best possible outcome. At Olson Concreting, we have over a decade of experience pouring concrete across Geelong, from the waterfront to the western suburbs, and we know exactly how to work with the local climate to deliver lasting results. Get in touch today to discuss your project and find the perfect time to pour in Geelong.

blogPosts.title: Exposed Aggregate vs Plain Concrete: A Geelong Homeowner Guide
blogPosts.excerpt: Choosing between exposed aggregate and plain concrete for your Geelong property? We compare costs, durability, aesthetics, and maintenance to help you decide.
body: When it comes to choosing a finish for your new concrete driveway or patio in Geelong, two options consistently come up: exposed aggregate and plain concrete. Both are popular choices across the region, and both have their strengths. But which one is right for your home? The answer depends on your budget, your home's style, how much maintenance you are willing to do, and the overall look you want to achieve. At Olson Concreting, we install both finishes regularly for Geelong homeowners, and we have put together this guide to help you make an informed decision for your next concrete project.

Plain concrete, sometimes called brushed or trowelled concrete, is the most straightforward and affordable option for Geelong driveways. It involves pouring a standard concrete slab and finishing the surface with a broom or trowel to create a smooth or lightly textured finish. The result is a clean, uniform surface that suits most home styles across Geelong. Plain concrete typically costs between $5,000 and $8,000 for a standard double driveway in the Geelong area. It is quick to install, easy to maintain, and provides a hard-wearing surface that can last decades when properly installed and sealed by an experienced local concreter.

Exposed aggregate concrete takes a very different approach to the finish. After the concrete is poured, the top layer of cement paste is carefully washed away to reveal the natural stones and pebbles embedded within the mix. This creates a textured, visually striking surface that adds instant kerb appeal to any Geelong property. Exposed aggregate driveways in Geelong typically cost between $8,000 and $14,000, depending on the size of the area and the type of aggregate selected. Popular choices among Geelong homeowners include river pebbles, granite chips, and basalt, each offering a different colour palette and texture.

Durability is a key consideration for Geelong homeowners, and both finishes perform well when installed correctly by a qualified concreter. Plain concrete is inherently strong and, when properly reinforced and sealed, can handle heavy vehicles and daily traffic for 20 to 30 years or more in the Geelong climate. Exposed aggregate is equally durable, and the textured surface provides natural slip resistance — a real advantage during Geelong's wet winter months when smooth concrete can become dangerously slippery. Both options meet Australian Standard AS 3600 for concrete construction, so durability alone is not the deciding factor between the two finishes.

Maintenance is where the two finishes start to differ noticeably for Geelong property owners. Plain concrete is easy to clean with a simple hose-down and benefits from resealing every two to three years to maintain its appearance and protect against staining from oil, leaves, or rust. Exposed aggregate requires slightly more attention because the textured surface can trap leaves, dirt, and debris in the crevices between the stones. A regular sweep and occasional pressure wash keeps exposed aggregate looking its best. Resealing is also recommended every two to three years to protect the aggregate and maintain the colour, particularly in Geelong's coastal suburbs where salt air can accelerate fading.

So, which should you choose for your Geelong home? If you want an affordable, low-maintenance finish that looks clean and modern, plain concrete is an excellent choice that will serve you well for decades. If you want to elevate your home's kerb appeal with a premium, textured surface that stands out in the neighbourhood, exposed aggregate is well worth the additional investment. At Olson Concreting, we help Geelong homeowners choose the right finish for their property, budget, and lifestyle every day. We provide free on-site quotes across Geelong and the surrounding suburbs, so get in touch to discuss your next concrete project.

blogPosts.title: Signs Your Geelong Concrete Driveway Needs Repair or Replacement
blogPosts.excerpt: Not sure whether to repair or replace your concrete driveway in Geelong? Learn the warning signs and when it is time to call a professional.
body: A well-built concrete driveway can last 20 to 30 years or more, but even the best driveways in Geelong eventually show signs of wear and age. The region's coastal climate, reactive clay soils, and daily traffic all take their toll on concrete surfaces over time. The question many Geelong homeowners face is whether a targeted repair will fix the problem or whether it is time for a full replacement. Ignoring early warning signs can lead to bigger, more expensive problems down the track that could have been avoided. Here is how to tell when your Geelong concrete driveway needs professional attention, and what your options are for fixing it properly.

The most obvious sign that your driveway needs attention is cracking. Hairline cracks are common in older concrete driveways across Geelong and are often cosmetic rather than structural. These can usually be filled and sealed relatively affordably by a local concreter. However, if you notice cracks wider than three millimetres, or cracks that are spreading rapidly across the surface, this may indicate underlying ground movement — a common issue in Geelong's clay soil suburbs like Belmont, Highton, and Grovedale. These wider cracks often mean the sub-base has been compromised, and a simple patch will not provide a lasting solution for your Geelong driveway.

Uneven or sunken sections are another serious red flag that Geelong homeowners should watch for. If water pools on your driveway instead of draining away naturally, or if you notice that one section has dropped lower than the surrounding concrete, you likely have a sub-base failure. In Geelong, this is often caused by poor compaction during the original installation, water erosion beneath the slab, or the natural movement of reactive clay soils that shift with seasonal moisture changes. While mudjacking or levelling can sometimes correct minor unevenness, significant sinking usually means the slab needs to be removed and replaced with proper ground preparation and drainage.

Surface deterioration is another warning sign that Geelong homeowners should not ignore or delay addressing. If the surface of your driveway is becoming rough, pitted, or starting to flake away in small chunks, this condition is known as spalling. Spalling is typically caused by water penetration into the concrete surface, freeze-thaw cycles, or a poor-quality concrete mix used during the original installation. In Geelong's coastal suburbs, salt air can accelerate this surface breakdown considerably. Small areas of spalling can sometimes be repaired with a concrete resurfacing product, but widespread surface damage usually means the concrete has reached the end of its useful life and needs full replacement.

Age is the final factor every Geelong homeowner should consider when weighing repair versus replacement. If your driveway is more than 20 years old and is showing multiple signs of wear across different areas, repair may only be a temporary fix that delays the inevitable. The cost of repeated repairs can quickly add up, and an old driveway with a failing sub-base will continue to deteriorate regardless of surface treatments applied. A full replacement allows you to address all the underlying issues at once — proper ground preparation, modern steel reinforcement, updated drainage solutions, and a fresh finish that complements your home. For many Geelong homeowners, a replacement driveway is the most cost-effective long-term investment.

If you are unsure whether your Geelong driveway needs a targeted repair or a full replacement, the best step is to get a professional assessment from an experienced local concreter. We will assess your driveway's condition, identify the underlying cause of any problems, and give you an honest recommendation on the most cost-effective solution. Whether it is a targeted repair or a brand-new driveway, we have the experience, equipment, and local knowledge to get it done right. Contact us today to book your free Geelong driveway assessment.
